chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Joining Local 802 in 1929
summary: He joined in March 1929 after a reading test; black and white musicians shared one union, with Petrillo as president.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, what was the union like. When did you first join a union, 802?
I joined in March 1929.
They had unions back then?
They sure did.
What were they like? Everybody had to join, of course?
Oh, yeah. I was supposed to join in '28 but first then they would test to see if you could read, give you a piece of music and send you across the hall.
And all of the bands had to -
(END OF REEL)
- separate? It was all one union here?
All one.
White and black belonged to the same local?
They did a little fighting in there... Pinky I don't know if you know him. He was a drummer. So you know,
one musician is a Negro, want to be this and one want to be something else - boy, they had a fight down there one day.
And what happened?
Nothing. Nobody won and everybody won. So now they have the Negros working down there just like the whites.
But both white and black belonged to the same union at the time?
Oh, yes.
Did you know Kenneth Rodne? He's a union official now. He used to have a band, I think, back -
Petrillo was the president when I joined.
Petrillo was the president?
Yeah.
Did they enforce the laws very strict at that time?
Not like now, no, no, no.
